region.text: the Minsk lands that Gleb Vseslavich received

ledger.note: 1101: Minsk becomes a principality under Gleb Vseslavich when Polotsk is divided. 'After Vseslav of Polotsk died in 1101, Polotsk was split into six principalities, and Gleb Vseslavich received the Minsk lands'; infobox 'Established: 1101'. The page names the land only by its river basins; the region is Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: Minsk and Slutsk, besieged and sacked in Monomakh's war

ledger.note: 1116: Vladimir Monomakh of Kiev besieges Minsk. 'Gleb fought Vladimir II Monomakh of Kiev and sacked Slutsk. Monomakh besieged Minsk for two months, and Gleb agreed to a peace treaty.' In 1117 Gleb attacked Smolensk and Monomakh's son Mstislav 'besieged and took Minsk' and took Gleb to Kiev.

region.text: Minsk after Gleb's death in Kiev

ledger.note: September 1119: Gleb dies a prisoner in Kiev and Minsk passes under Kievan influence. 'September 1119: Gleb died in Kiev'; 'After 1119 the principality fell under Kievan influence'. The page gives no separate date for the capture of Minsk, so the end of the contest is read from Gleb's death; the widow ruled until 1158 and the principality was independent again by 1164 (battle against Polotsk).

region.text: Drutsk, 'entirely taken over by the Principality of Minsk'

ledger.note: 1260: Minsk absorbs Drutsk. The Drutsk page: 'Drutsk was entirely taken over by the Principality of Minsk' in the second half of the 13th century (no year); the Minsk page lists 'the historical town of Drutsk' among Minsk's towns. 1260 is the first year of Cliopatria's enlarged Minsk shape.

region.text: the Principality of Minsk, annexed de facto by Lithuania

ledger.note: 1326: Minsk passes to the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. 'Vasily, ruler of Minsk, signed a treaty between Lithuania and Novgorod for Prince Gediminas'; the lead gives 1326 as the date of de facto annexation and the infobox as the disestablishment year. The body text instead has the principality 'cease to exist' after the Union of Horodło in 1413.
1326: the Principality of Minsk ends, annexed de facto by the Grand Duchy of Lithuania (infobox 'Disestablished: 1326'); it becomes the Minsk Voivodeship after 1413.

wars.name: Monomakh's war against Gleb of Minsk
wars.outcome: Monomakh besieged Minsk for two months in 1116 and a peace was made; after Gleb's attack on Smolensk in 1117 Mstislav took Minsk and carried Gleb to Kiev, where he died in September 1119; Minsk fell under Kievan influence.
wars.note: The page gives no separate year for the capture of Minsk.

wars.name: Minsk and Drutsk against Polotsk (1164)
wars.outcome: With Lithuanian help Volodar of Minsk won a battle against the prince of Polotsk, which affirmed the principality's independence.
wars.note: The Vitebsk page adds a 1162 quarrel among the princes of Vitebsk, Minsk and Drutsk over control of Polotsk; no territorial result on either page.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Rus' (Minsk escapes)
wars.outcome: Minsk escaped the invasion of 1237-1239; in 1249 a combined Minsk and Lithuanian army repelled a Tatar-Mongol invasion.

certainty.note: The pages give river basins and town lists, never a frontier line; the Drutsk and Vitebsk borders in particular are approximate.

notes: Pages opened: 4 of up to 5. Infobox area: none on the Minsk page; the Cliopatria areas could not be compared. CLIOPATRIA ROW: 1260-1313 is not Minsk alone. Its 98.8 k km2 is the Minsk shape plus all of Cliopatria's Drutsk and Vitebsk shapes (the Vitebsk shape also holds Polotsk), measured on the grid; the Vitebsk page keeps Vitebsk a separate principality until 1320, so the dossier removes it (keyframe corrections 1260-1313) and keeps Drutsk (taken over by Minsk in the second half of the 13th century; year 1260 is Cliopatria's). The grand-duchy-of-lithuania dossier should note that its Minsk vassal_start is dated 1250 at confidence 1 while the Minsk page says 'nominally annexed by the Grand Duchy of Lithuania in 1242' and calls the princes 'virtually vassals' in the 13th century. END: the page gives two ends, 1326 (lead: de facto annexation; infobox) and 1413 (Union of Horodlo). The dossier ends in 1326 and bridges 1314-1326 at confidence 1; the Lithuanian dossier has the gain and vassal_end in 1314 (Cliopatria's year), a conflict for the reviewer: the page's year is 1326. Not settled: no page opened gives the frontier at any date; the 1146-1165 Rostislav Glebovich entry in the infobox is not in the text; Minsk under Kievan influence 1119-1164 would be a vassal relation in the Kievan Rus' dossier.
